mappings.note: Both contain the superscription: 'To the choir director. On Gittit. Of Asaf.' (Norwegian) / Hebrew equivalent.
Both contain: 'Sing joyfully to God our strength...'
Both contain instructions for instruments (tambourine, lyre, harp).
Both mention blowing the horn at new moon and full moon.
Both state it is a statute for Israel/judgment of Jacob's God.
Both mention the testimony in Joseph and hearing an unknown language.
Both describe removing the burden from shoulders/hands leaving baskets.
Both contain: 'In distress you called... answered in thunder... tested at Meribah.' Includes Sela.
Both say: 'Hear my people... if only you would listen to me.'
Both forbid strange gods and worshiping foreign deities.
Both identify God as the one who brought them out of Egypt and say 'Open your mouth wide...'
Both state: 'But my people did not listen... Israel would not have me.'
Both describe letting them go in the stubbornness of their heart.
Both express: 'Oh that my people would listen... walk in my ways.'
Both mention humbling enemies and turning hand against adversaries.
Translation verse 16 contains only the first half of OSMAIN v16 ('Those who hate the Lord...'). The second part about food is in Translation v17.
Translation verse 17 contains the second half of OSMAIN v16 ('I would feed them with finest wheat...'). This is a split from Translation v16.
